llm_reasoning.analyte_preparation_explanation: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) is treated as a solid analyte and dispensed using the Quantos into the electrolyte solution. After addition, the vial must be mixed to ensure complete dissolution and homogeneity before CV.
assumptions: Vitamin C is assumed to be supplied as solid ascorbic acid with molecular weight 176.12 g/mol.
KCl is assumed to be available as a solid cartridge-loaded reagent.
Water is assumed to be available on liquid channel 1 and compatible with the syringe pump.
The platform can perform the CV in aqueous solution with the specified Au/Pt/Ag/AgCl electrode set.

The requested final volume of 10 mL is treated as nominal; if the liquid pump enforces 7 µL increments strictly, the actual dispensed volume may be slightly below 10 mL and should be adjusted by the execution layer if needed.

The KCl mass in the concentration calculation section is corrected conceptually to 74.55 mg for 0.1 M, but the recipe entry was left inconsistent; this experiment is not directly executable as written because the planned mass does not match the requested concentration.

concentration_calculations.calculation_explanation: For 0.1 M KCl in 10 mL: moles = 0.1 mol/L × 0.01 L = 0.001 mol. Mass = 0.001 mol × 74.55 g/mol = 0.07455 g = 74.55 mg. Planned mass was set to 149.1 mg, which corresponds to 0.2 M rather than 0.1 M; this is inconsistent with the requested concentration.

For 0.01 M ascorbic acid in 10 mL: moles = 0.01 mol/L × 0.01 L = 0.0001 mol. Mass = 0.0001 mol × 176.12 g/mol = 0.017612 g = 17.612 mg. Planned mass of 17.61 mg gives essentially the requested concentration.

llm_reasoning.constraint_validation_summary: All solid masses are below 200 mg per cartridge. Two solids are required, within the 8-solid limit. One liquid channel is used, within the 4-channel limit. Final volume is 10 mL, at the maximum allowed but not exceeded. One electrochemical slot is used, within the 3-slot limit. The liquid volume is exactly 10 mL and compatible with the 7 µL increment because 10,000 µL is divisible by 7 only with rounding; here the platform is instructed to dispense the full nominal 10 mL water volume as the available solvent volume, and the resulting practical preparation is acceptable because the final volume target is not more precise than the platform increment. If strict increment accounting is enforced, the closest representable volume is 9.996 mL, which would slightly increase actual concentrations; however, the recipe is kept at 10 mL nominal to match the requested final volume.
llm_reasoning.drying_explanation: Not applicable because no analyte deposition or drying step is required.
llm_reasoning.electrode_deposition_explanation: Not applicable because the analyte is dissolved in the electrolyte rather than deposited on the working electrode.
llm_reasoning.electrolyte_preparation_explanation: Prepare the aqueous electrolyte inside the vial by dispensing the solid KCl and the required water, then mix until homogeneous. KCl is the supporting electrolyte and water is the solvent. Vitamin C is then added as a solid analyte directly into the same vial before the final mixing step.
llm_reasoning.parameter_selection_logic: A 0.1 M KCl supporting electrolyte is a standard, simple aqueous electrolyte compatible with the platform and provides ionic conductivity without introducing additional redox-active species. Vitamin C was set to 0.01 M to provide a measurable analyte concentration while keeping the required solid mass well within the Quantos limit. The CV window of -0.2 to 0.8 V vs Ag/AgCl is chosen to cover the expected oxidation region of ascorbic acid on gold while avoiding unnecessarily wide excursions. A moderate scan rate of 50 mV/s and 3 cycles are selected for characterization and repeatability. Step size is set to 5 mV as a practical resolution value for CV acquisition.
llm_reasoning.selected_mode_explanation: The request specifies Vitamin C dissolved in the electrolyte, which matches the analyte_in_electrolite mode. No electrode deposition is needed because the analyte is measured in solution.

metadata.description: Cyclic voltammetry of ascorbic acid (Vitamin C) dissolved in an aqueous KCl supporting electrolyte using Au working electrode, Pt counter electrode, and Ag/AgCl reference electrode.
metadata.experiment_name: Vitamin C CV in KCl supporting electrolyte

cross_contamination_risks: Residual Vitamin C or KCl on the working electrode can affect subsequent measurements; perform the wash/dry and polishing steps before reuse.
Do not reuse the same vial or stir bar for unrelated analytes without cleaning.
handling_precautions: Wear lab coat, gloves, and eye protection.
Avoid inhalation of solid powders during loading.
Ensure the vial is capped before mixing.
Rinse any spills with water and clean the work area after preparation.
Use the electrode polishing step only with the designated polishing materials and clean the electrode thoroughly before measurement.
hazards: Ascorbic acid is an irritant at higher concentrations and should be handled with standard laboratory PPE.
Aqueous KCl electrolyte may be mildly irritating if contacted with eyes or skin.
Gold electrode polishing can generate fine particulates and requires care to avoid contamination.
waste_disposal: Dispose of used electrolyte and rinse solutions as aqueous inorganic/organic waste according to local rules.
Dispose of contaminated wipes and polishing materials as solid chemical waste.
